decisions.reason: Active ‘politicians made use of other people’s fame’ is more natural than the passive Korean-shaped ‘a person’s fame was used’.
SOL naturalizes the five chin folds and 상상하니, but ‘pouting’ breaks the 삐지다/sulk callback; BASE’s ‘five-chin-folded’ is calqued.
decisions.replacement: What was there to sulk about? Imagining a middle-aged man with five folds under his chin sulking sent goose bumps all over my body.

decisions.reason: ‘Bend over backward to please’ intensifies 비위를 살살 맞춰 줘야; careful flattery is the source action.
‘Wouldn’t I be better off’ is the natural first-person recast of 낫지 않을까.
Drops the calqued ‘someone who’ while keeping 냉큼 달려가야 하는 사람도 아니고.
SOL’s ‘home’ overspecifies 복귀하는 길, and dropping 성주라는 아저씨 flattens the dismissive label.
‘Let him sulk’ matches the jussive 많이 삐져라 better than ‘He could sulk’.
덥석 is the sudden taking of the invitation; ‘Snatch’ as the SFX is more precise than ‘Grab’.
잡은 is grabbed/caught; with 덥석 already as Snatch, snatched would double the theft sense.
‘Had turned cold’ recasts 방금과 다르게 싸늘한 without the stiff ‘unlike before’, and the combined sentence reads cleaner.
BASE’s ‘Oh my’ keeps 아이고 and ‘moved’ keeps 감격; SOL’s ‘of course not’ is the natural reply, but it weakens 아이고 and recasts 존경/감격.
decisions.replacement: “Oh my, of course not. It’s just that our Young Master has always respected the City Lord so deeply that he was too moved to speak.”

decisions.reason: Finite ‘turned his back and mouthed’ is cleaner English than the ‘having turned’ participle.
SOL drops 무조건 and the questioning 가라고?
Uses glossary Great Nation and ‘spoken like’ for 백성답구려.
SOL improves 얼굴을 펴고 흐뭇하게 웃은 but ‘turned to leave’ jumps ahead of 돌아섰다.
decisions.replacement: Only then did the county magistrate’s expression soften into a satisfied smile. He turned around.

decisions.reason: ‘Take that as your acceptance’ is idiomatic for 승낙한 것으로 알고, and ‘as well’ restores 에게도.
Removes BASE’s ungrammatical double article ‘the The’.
꾹 밟으며 is pressing down, not planting; SOL’s clause order before the whisper is the better English.
decisions.replacement: Once the county magistrate and the government troops had moved away, I pressed my foot down on Hyuk Mujin’s and whispered,

decisions.reason: Splitting off 응? as ‘Don’t you?’ preserves the menacing pause.
‘Let’s get out of here first’ is more spoken for 일단 … 빠져나간 후에.
SOL’s ‘continued until’ is less stiff than ‘proceeded’, but 꼬마 is little, not young.
decisions.replacement: We continued farther into the village until we reached our destination. A little errand boy shot out like a bullet and bowed at the waist.

decisions.reason: Two-sentence 한 번/두 번 rhythm is cleaner than BASE’s packed once/then clause.
본 적이 있는 is seen, not met.
Uses glossary silver nyang and spoken ‘Right?’ for 맞지?
어허 is Hey, not Why; the rhetorical 삿대질을 해? is ‘how dare you’, not a literal yes/no.
decisions.replacement: “Hey, you little brat. How dare you point at a guest as lofty as the heavens?”

decisions.reason: ‘Sternly scolding’ is cleaner than the calqued ‘in a stern voice’.
SOL’s 헛숨을 들이켰다 is right; it drops 꼬마.
decisions.replacement: The little boy glanced nervously between us, then sucked in a breath when he saw the pouch packed with silver.

decisions.reason: 접수한다 is the active ‘taking over’, which also sets up the gangster joke.
쌍칼 is the two-knife gangster image; SOL genericizes it to knife-wielding thug.
Both omit 허겁지겁 and 국물부터.
decisions.replacement: The three zombies climbed out of the carriage and began frantically gulping down the broth first the moment the food arrived.

decisions.reason: SOL drops 아니 and 하루도 쉬지 않고, and ‘senseless’ intensifies 과음.
잔소리가 날아들었다 is nagging flying at him; SOL flattens it to ‘began nagging’.
‘Letting them see you like this’ is more spoken for 이런 모습을 보이시면.
‘That single sentence’ ties the punchline without the stiff ‘With a single sentence’ opener.
냉큼 받아 버리는 is prompt/rash acceptance, not ‘jumped at’ the invitation.
SOL’s ‘huddled’ is unsupported, it drops 눈치만 살피고, and 쥐방울만 한 is tiny, not a mouse’s squeak.
Restores glossary Gate Guard Pavilion and 이라는 as ‘they call’.
‘Actual head’ is ordinary English for 실질적인 경영자; ‘de facto’ is Latinate without a fidelity gain.
맨날 is every day, and ‘bullied by’ is more natural than ‘bullied under’.
‘Keep helping’ is the spoken imperative for 도와주게.
그쪽 after the City Lord is ‘he’, and 겪어 본 is experienced; SOL swaps both for government/seen.
SOL adds unsupported ‘very’ and turns 알고 있느냐 into past ‘Did you know’.
‘Conventions’ is the natural English for 설정, without the calqued ‘here in the Murim’.
‘Nothing good can come’ matches 좋을 것이 없다, and ‘world itself’ sharpens the 천하/무림 contrast.
반쯤 차 있는 is half-filled, not ‘half a bowl of broth’.
있지 is possess/have; ‘wield’ changes the verb without a real prose gain.
Tighter, still faithful rendering of 치안을 맡기다 / 파견 / 상부상조.
악어새 is the crocodile-bird pairing; ‘plover’ replaces the transparent source image.
BASE’s ‘finally’ is extra; SOL’s ‘nagging’ captures 자꾸만 but drops 아까부터.
decisions.replacement: After thinking for a moment, I voiced the question that had been nagging at me since earlier.

decisions.reason: The omitted subject is the government, not Wikyung; Mukyung’s answer confirms it.
도 marks even Lee Cheonbaek; SOL wrongly attaches ‘even’ to killing children.
decisions.replacement: Even Lee Cheonbaek had massacred everyone at the Sakju Branch and committed the insane act of killing children, but the victims had belonged to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

decisions.reason: Preserves 할 수 있겠다 and 희생된; SOL makes it a definite ‘casualties’ statement.
Both drop 그런 거 없이; SOL also drops the 아닌가 tag.
decisions.replacement: But the mounted bandits killed indiscriminately and burned everything in their path without any of that, didn’t they?

decisions.reason: Present-tense general truth for 만만한 게 양민이니까, without the heavy ‘perspective’ calque.
Subjectless fragment matches the punchy 강자에게 약하고 proverb.
Keeps 중요한 건, names 마적, and 구경도 as ‘even’; SOL’s ‘a single’ is extra.
BASE underplays 툭 내뱉었다; SOL adds unsupported ‘without looking up’ and replaces comic 흡입.
decisions.replacement: Jin Wikyung let his voice trail off. Jin Mukyung, who had been silently inhaling his food until then, suddenly blurted,

decisions.reason: 건가? is a question; SOL turns it into ‘perhaps’.
경기를 일으켰다 is a fit, not ‘nearly’ a seizure.
어허 is Hey/tut, not ‘Now’.
‘Besides’ is the natural connective for 아니고요.
물었다 is asked; SOL’s ‘turned to’ drops it.
Spoken sarcastic gloss of 무능이라는 단어를 모르나, with the word marked.
삼족 is three clans, not three generations.
이 자식 is bastard, but 말발 is skill with words, not specifically talking back; SOL also shifts tense.
decisions.replacement: *This bastard Jin Mukyung has gotten pretty good with words.*

decisions.reason: ‘Current City Lord’ is the natural English for 지금 성주, not calqued ‘right now’.
Preserves the scolding repetition 모르면 모른다고.
성을 쓴다 is blunt ‘has the surname’; ‘bears’ is too literary for Mukyung.
Italics are the right spoken echo of 그래서.
‘Apparently’ matches 모양이다, and the time phrase leads more cleanly.
이런 일이 is ‘this sort of thing’; SOL’s bare ‘this’ is only a synonym swap.
‘Keep going’ is the spoken 계속해.
‘Let out a deep sigh’ matches 한숨을 푹 내쉰 better than ‘sighed deeply’.
BASE omits 억지로라도; SOL’s ‘far above’ intensifies 격이 달라.
decisions.replacement: “The current City Lord is the Emperor’s youngest brother, and his imperial title is Prince. As a direct member of the imperial family, he stands on a different level from the other City Lords. He’s someone whose invitation we must accept, even if we have to force ourselves, if only to preserve his dignity.”

decisions.reason: 무려 진짜 왕 is an actual king, no less; SOL’s ‘prince’ flattens the narrator’s joke.
‘His spoon was made of vibranium’ is cleaner than ‘He had a vibranium spoon’.
Complete sentence for 핵수저, 그 이상 rather than a hanging noun phrase.
왕씩이나 must stay king, not royalty; SOL’s tighter letter line is otherwise better.
decisions.replacement: “Then how can someone who’s practically a king be so incompetent? One letter to his brother should get him all the support he needs from above. Are they on bad terms?”

decisions.reason: ‘His immediately older brother’ is cleaner than BASE’s calqued appositive.
살인도 일어나는데 is that murder happens, not that people kill each other.
다시 한번 경기를 일으켰다 is another fit, not ‘nearly’ a seizure.
판관님 is courtroom ‘Your Honor’, but 오래전부터 is a long time, not ‘deaf for years’.
decisions.replacement: “Your Honor, I didn’t hear anything. I truly know nothing. In fact, I haven’t been able to hear for a long time…”

decisions.reason: ‘Wine and women’ is the natural collocation for 술과 여자 ahead of 주지육림.
Echoes 술 as wine, matching the following 주지육림 line.
피식 is a short scoffing laugh, not a quiet one.
너무 이른 나이 is too early; ‘a bit young’ weakens it.
뭐, 열 살? is ‘What, ten?’, one beat, not ‘What? Ten?’
‘Could become far more’ captures 그 이상도 될 수 있는 more directly than ‘has the bloodline to become more’.
아저씨 continues the middle-aged-man joke; ‘grown man’ drops that callback.
Restores 에도 as even a falling leaf.
Spoken ‘What’s even more amusing’ for 더 재밌는 사실.
더 무능한 is more incompetent, not ‘the incompetent one’.
구멍가게 is a corner shop, not a convenience store; SOL’s ‘anything’ overreaches 제대로 돌아갈 리.
decisions.replacement: This wasn’t some neighborhood corner store. They had put a child in a position that demanded ability and responsibility. There was no way things could run properly.

decisions.reason: ‘His answer was unexpected’ is tighter for 뜻밖의 대답이 돌아왔다.
슈퍼 루키 is super rookie, including 떠오르는 as rising; ‘hot new’ drops the loanword.
SOL adds unsupported ‘twisted’ and drops the 표정으로 말한다 beat.
개 같았다 is ‘it was fucking awful’; BASE’s ‘nightmare’ swaps in a different metaphor.
